registry.description: Love is the most foundational and most theologically dense word in the entire corpus. The Hebrew and Greek vocabulary spans a vast range: the steadfast covenant love of God (hesed), the deep personal affection (ahava), the tender compassion (racham), the Greek agape (self-giving, willed, unconditional love), phileo (warm affection), and eros (passion and longing). God is love: not merely loving but constituted by it. Human love is modelled on and enabled by divine love. Everything else in the moral life is an expression of love rightly ordered.
registry.sb_classification_reasoning: Love at its fullest is received from outside the human person — poured into hearts by the Spirit (Rom 5:5), preceded by God's prior love (1Jo 4:19). This is spirit-primary in origin. As experienced and exercised, love operates characteristically at the soul level — the settled disposition of the inner life, the affective-volitional orientation of the heart. Love's bodily expression (kiss, embrace, tears, running) is regular and genuine but secondary — it manifests love rather than constituting it. Classification: Spirit-Soul Interface. Confidence: High.
